messages.subject: Re: RJMCMC for multiple models
parts:
Hi Miki,

Thanks for posting the question.

I can't run your code because I don't have your `data` or your `d_log_inf`.

Can you clarify what you're trying to do here? With nimble's RJ tools, managed at a high level from configureRJ and implemented in several nimbleFunctions, you wouldn't need to write your own. Of course you can, but I am not sure if they are trying to provide different functionality.

Can you say what version of nimble you're using? I'd suggest either providing a fully reproducible example (you can share data off-list if you prefer) or clarifying your goals.

Post-processing results from RJ can sometimes be confusing at first because you'll have a chain that sometimes sits at zero and sometimes samples a non-zero posterior region.

For reference on this thread, the published version of the paper you linked seems to be here.

Perry


On Sun, Jan 19, 2025 at 11:44 PM Miki <yira...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Nimble users,

I am using Nimble to implement reversible jump MCMC (RJMCMC) for a nested model involving two variables: delta_1 and delta_2. My goal is to select among the following four models:

  1. Neither delta_1 nor delta_2 included
  2. Only delta_1 included
  3. Only delta_2 included
  4. Both delta_1 and delta_2 included
Following the example in the Nimble manual, I wrote an RJ sampler and a RW_sampler_nonzero for both delta_1 and delta_2. My understanding is that the algorithm alternates between the two variables: proposing to add a parameter if it is zero, or proposing to remove it if it is nonzero. From my reading (https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01340), this approach resembles "nonreversible jump" MCMC. 
The results are promising overall, with the model correctly identifying the true model used to simulate the data—except for the fourth model (both delta_1 and delta_2), which seems to suffer from identifiability issues even in standard MCMC settings.
However, I’m encountering convergence issues when assessing the chains using Brooks' chi-square tests (https://www.jstor.org/stable/1391067). The p-values don’t increase steadily as simulations progress, and sometimes the chains fail to converge.

My questions are:

  1. Could there be an issue with the RJMCMC implementation for the nested model?
  2. Should I introduce constraints to avoid cases where both delta_1 and delta_2 are nonzero to address identifiability problems?

Below is the RJMCMC part of my code (d_log_inf is a user-defined function):

Code <- nimbleCode({
  alpha ~ dgamma(1.5, 1)
  beta ~ dgamma(2, 3)
  delta1 ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  delta2 ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  #constraint_data ~ dconstraint(delta1 + delta2 <= max(delta1, delta2))
  inf_time[1:N] ~ d_log_inf(N, position_y[1:N], position_x[1:N], t_start, t_end, alpha, beta, delta1, delta2)
})


##Nimble model
Model <- nimbleModel(Code,
                     data = list(position_y = data$position_y,
                                 position_x = data$position_x,
                                 inf_time = data$time_of_infected
                                 #constraint_data = 1),
                     constants = list(N = 100, t_start = 1, t_end = 50),
                     inits = list(alpha = 5, beta = 2, delta1 = 0.001, delta2 = 0))

#Non-zero sampler
RW_sampler_nonzero <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    regular_RW_sampler <- sampler_RW(model, mvSaved, target = target, control = control$RWcontrol)
    fixedValue <- control$fixedValue
  },
  run = function() { 
    if(model[[target]] != fixedValue) regular_RW_sampler$run()
  },
  methods = list(
    reset = function() {regular_RW_sampler$reset()}
  ))
#RJ sampler
RJsampler <- nimbleFunction(
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function( model, mvSaved, target, control ) {
    fixedValue <- control$fixedValue
    scale <- control$scale
    logRatioProbFixedOverProbNotFixed <- log(control$prior) - log(1-control$prior)
    calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
  },
  run = function( ) { 
    currentValue <- model[[target]]
    currentLogProb <- model$getLogProb(calcNodes)
    if(currentValue != fixedValue) { 
       logProbReverseProposal <- dbeta(currentValue, 1, 1, log = TRUE)
      model[[target]] <<- fixedValue
      proposalLogProb <- model$calculate(calcNodes)
      log_accept_prob <- proposalLogProb - currentLogProb - logRatioProbFixedOverProbNotFixed + logProbReverseProposal
    } else {
      proposalValue <- rbeta(1, 1, 1)
      model[[target]] <<- proposalValue
      logProbForwardProposal <- dbeta(proposalValue, 1, 1, log = TRUE)
      proposalLogProb <- model$calculate(calcNodes)
      log_accept_prob <- proposalLogProb - currentLogProb + logRatioProbFixedOverProbNotFixed - logProbForwardProposal
    }
    accept <- decide(log_accept_prob)
    if(accept) {
      copy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
    } else {
      copy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodes, logProb = TRUE)
    }
  },
  methods = list(reset = function() {
  })
)
#Configure and add sampler
mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(Model)
mcmcConf$removeSamplers('delta1')
mcmcConf$removeSamplers('delta2')
mcmcConf$addSampler(target = 'delta1',
                    type = 'RJsampler',
                    control = list(fixedValue = 0, prior = 0.5, scale = 0.1))
mcmcConf$addSampler(target = 'delta1',
                    type = 'RW_sampler_nonzero',
                    control = list(fixedValue = 0,
                                   RWcontrol = list(adaptive = TRUE,
                                                    adaptInterval = 100,
                                                    scale = 0.3,
                                                    log = FALSE,
                                                    reflective = FALSE)))
mcmcConf$addSampler(target = 'delta2',
                    type = 'RJsampler',
                    control = list(fixedValue = 0, prior = 0.5, scale = 0.1))
mcmcConf$addSampler(target = 'delta2',
                    type = 'RW_sampler_nonzero',
                    control = list(fixedValue = 0,
                                   RWcontrol = list(adaptive = TRUE,
                                                    adaptInterval = 100,
                                                    scale = 0.3,
                                                    log = FALSE,
                                                    reflective = FALSE)))
mcmc <- buildMCMC(mcmcConf)
compiled <- compileNimble(Model, mcmc, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

Best regards,
Miki
